content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper presents some empirical explorations on differentially private learning over some image classification datasets, under the framework of pretraining on public dataset then finetuning on private dataset. The state-of-the-art performance is achieved by tuning optimizers and last layer finetuning.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
The main strength is the comprehensive experiment report and ablation study of how different components in experiments can affect the final performance.

The main weakness is the limited novelty, the paper is a combination of experiment results with tricks commonly used in the community.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper tackles the problem of private fine-tuning of vision models, and proposes a series of tricks to improve the performance of such models. Specifically, the authors investigate some known recipes (large batch sizes, larger models pre-trained on larger datasets) and propose new improvements (using the LAMB optimizer, zero-init of the last layer, one-step optimization). Experiments are conducted mainly on Imagenet (although some CIFAR-10/100 results are also provided), and show that the proposed approach leads to state-of-the-art performance. The results also show that DP-LAMB is superior to DP-SGD for fine-tuning vision models such as ViT and ResNet.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths
- The paper tackles an interesting problem, namely obtaining accurate models trained with privacy
- The paper provides some interesting results, such as the fact that zero-init beats random init for the last layer, or the fact that one step fine-tuning yields great results

Weaknesses
- Sidestepping DP: it is important for the privacy community to show numbers comparable to the non-private SOTA, and this paper contributes to this effort. However, most of the gains are actually when sidestepping DP: the (large) model is pre-trained on a very large dataset (300M to 4B images) on which it learns its features and probably most of the concepts (18k to 29k classes).
- Non-reproducibility: while this paper puts some effort in showing numbers for a variety of architectures and training setups (last layer / full), having a competitive benchmark based on a secret dataset prevents outsiders from comparing and/or competing.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper has a clear flow although some of the technicalities make it a dense read. It is very well executed, with clear experiments and extensive ablations. To the best of my knowledge, using LAMB in the context of DP is new as well as single-step tuning of the last layer. With the exception of a handful of side experiments, the paper is mostly not reproducible as its main ingredient is pre-training on JFT, which is a non-public dataset.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper shows that private fine-tuning can come very close to non-private performance for Imagenet. Furthermore, the proposed methods (DP-LAMB and single step finetuning) are interesting and to the best of my knowledge new. I am a bit on the fence for this paper as it will not be reproducible and most of the effort relies on bypassing private training. I still lean towards accept as some of the contributions for fine-tuning seem important, and the final results can help promote privacy.
content.correctness: 4: All of the claims and statements are well-supported and correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper empirically studies differentially private image classification models and explores factors such as model size, batch size, and optimizers for privately finetuning pre-trained image models on large public datasets. Through experiments, this paper finds that performance can be boosted by increasing pretraining data and model size, batch size, and tweaking initialization.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:

This paper provides comprehensive experiments for exploring multiple factors in finetuning large models with privacy guarantees and provides positive experimental results.
This paper is easy to follow.

Weakness:
1. This paper didn’t provide new approaches regarding improving DP utility to the community. The method that finetunes pre-trained models with DP optimizer is not new. Exploring hyper-parameters in the experiment is a proof of concept without much novelty.
2. There is a lack of in-depth explanation for some empirical results observed in this paper. It is observed that the last layer finetune is better than the full model finetune. Would it be due to reduced noise variance in the last layer finetune? Also, why DP LAMB is much better than DP SGD? 
3. Some results need more justification. Some of the accuracy gaps between different settings in Table 4 are minor (less than 1%) which could be caused by variance. It will be good to report variance with repeated runs (different random seeds).
4. The experiment can be enhanced by considering more sets of privacy parameters. Most experiments in the paper only reported private results on one set of privacy parameters which makes it hard to draw a conclusion.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is easy to follow. There is not much novelty in this paper. The experiments could be reproducible with the details provided in this paper.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper just explored hyper-parameters in finetuning large models with differential privacy. Overall, don’t find much novelty in this paper. This submission is not ready for ICLR. Thus, I recommend reject.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 1: The contributions are neither significant nor novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper conduct some empircal study on using DP-SGD in image classification tasks. This paper conclude some useful strategies, including large batchsize, large scale public pre-training with small scale privacy fine-tuning. The performance on the image classification task (with DP requirement) is significant.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Pros:
1. The privacy protection reflected in this paper reach a meaningful strength, that is, the \espilon reach a meaning level (<10).
2. The performance on the image classification task (with DP requirement) is significant. The improvement is amazing.

Cons:
1. Some of the conclusions are also verified in other papers (even if some of them comes from NLP with DP-SGD). For example,  [Xuechen Li' ICLR'22] and [Da Yu' ICLR'22] applied DP-SGD to the pretrain-finetune paradigm and also tried large batchsize (up to 2048). (Besides, Xuechen Li' ICLR'22 also propose a cliping method to reduce the GPU memory so that the model can run with large batchsize). As DP-SGD is kind of model-agnostic (agnostic for most gradient based learning models), the experiences from NLP with DP-SGD can also be used in image easily. 

2. The baselines are too weak. The proposed model is only compared with non-privacy methods but does not compared with DP-based or DP-SGD based methods. Please consider some strong DP baselines in image classification. Since this paper also use "large batchsize" and pretrain-finetune, it may be better to compare with [Xuechen Li' ICLR'22] and [Da Yu' ICLR'22].

3. This paper did not propose some interesting or new technical modules or strategies, so the technical contribution to the commiunity is quite limited.

4. The paper organization can be improved. It's kind of weird that there is no "method" section. 


Xuechen Li, Florian Tramèr, Percy Liang, and Tatsunori Hashimoto. Large language models can be strong differentially private learners. In ICLR, 2022. This paper was published at ICLR'22 instead of arxiv only.

Da Yu, Saurabh Naik, Arturs Backurs, Sivakanth Gopi, Huseyin A Inan, Gautam Kamath, Janardhan Kulkarni, Yin Tat Lee, Andre Manoel, Lukas Wutschitz, et al. Differentially private fine-tuning of language models. In ICLR, 2022
content.summary_of_the_review: I think this paper is useful to the community in terms of the exprical study, but the technical novel is limited. I tend to reject this paper.
